name: Nympha
title: Host of the church in Laodicea
summary: Nympha was a Christian woman who opened her home in Laodicea (or a nearby area) for church meetings. She is mentioned by the apostle Paul in Colossians as an important contributor to the growth of the early church by making her house available to the community. Although she is only briefly mentioned, her mention testifies to the important role women played in the early Christian movement.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned by Paul in Colossians
keyEvents.description: Paul sends greetings to Nympha and the church that meets in her house, showing that she was a recognized and respected leader in the Christian community.

keyEvents.title: Host of the house church
keyEvents.description: Nympha made her own home available as a meeting place for believers, which was crucial for the organization of the early church when there were no dedicated church buildings.

keyEvents.title: The letter is to be shared with Laodicea
keyEvents.description: Paul instructs the Colossians to share the letter with the church in Laodicea and with Nympha's house church, highlighting the connection between various early congregations.

keyEvents.title: Part of a network of early Christian leaders
keyEvents.description: Nympha is mentioned alongside other co-workers such as Archippus, placing her within a broader network of Christian leaders in the Lycus Valley.
